title: Pour Records
brief: Cube results for Meridian Build pour {{pour}} (level 3 columns) came back below the specified strength. You need to trace the pour records and define which elements and pours are affected. You have 12 visit points.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Other pours from the same mix and day
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Cube results for {{pour}}: 28-day strength 31 against 35 specified; recorded and reported promptly.
Curing tank log shows the heater failed for 3 days during the cubes' curing; no note of impact.
evidence.whyItMatters: Test conditions must be controlled; otherwise results may not reflect the concrete.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check test conditions before trusting a result.

evidence.text: Delivery tickets: 6 trucks for {{pour}}; ticket T-5 has no time of addition of water recorded and a mix code differing from the others.
evidence.whyItMatters: Delivery records must show what was placed and where.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read every ticket in the pour.

evidence.text: The same mix on the same day also went to pour P-209 (level 3 slab edge); its location on the element register is "level 3, various".
evidence.whyItMatters: Elements must be traceable to their pour.
evidence.missedExplanation: Find other pours from the same mix and day.

evidence.text: Pour record for {{pour}} does not record which column received which truck.
evidence.whyItMatters: Records needed to trace work must be kept.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check that pour records map trucks to elements.

evidence.text: Element register lists the 12 columns in {{pour}}.
Concrete supplier is approved and evaluated 4 months ago.
Cube press verification is 10 days overdue (label LP-3).
evidence.whyItMatters: Overdue verification weakens confidence; review recent results.

evidence.text: Site engineer: "The driver added water to truck T-5 to help placing. Nobody recorded it." (note 9)
evidence.whyItMatters: Changes to the product during placement must be controlled and recorded.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what happened on the day.

evidence.text: Pour sequence chart is hand-drawn but current.

options: All 12 columns of {{pour}}, the slab edge elements of P-209 from the same mix and day, and a review of cube results tested during the curing heater failure
None; retest the cubes and wait
decisions.rationale: The mix, the day, and the test conditions widen the scope.

containment: Stop loading on affected elements until assessed; identify P-209 element locations
correction: Commission in-place testing of affected elements and decide disposition with the designer and client
cause: Pour records do not map trucks to elements, site water additions are not controlled, and curing conditions are not monitored
corrective: Add truck-to-element mapping and water addition control to the pour record, and alarm the curing tank
effectiveness: Audit the next ten pour records

debriefText.found: You traced the pour to trucks, elements, and test conditions.
debriefText.missed: The other pour from the same mix and day is often missed.
debriefText.falseFinding: A hand-drawn current chart is conforming.
